notes:
PASS on the fake backend. The package serves the card's first model, sim/digit_sim/digit-v3-box-tower-of-hanoi.xml (Digit, the upstream default --robot at eval.py:12 and README.md:47), as a MujocoDriver in simulated R0: cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action.ctrl}, with every ctrl element checked against the model's 20 motor actuator_ctrlrange intervals before data.ctrl is written, and cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults (mj_resetData). The card's g1 and h1 MJCF scenes are not served: one MujocoDriver serves one model file, and models[0] is the default robot. WHAT IS NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself was not installed and could not be installed where the gate ran (no network, no pip). The fake backend (fake.py) is a stand-in for the mujoco library: it parses the MJCF text for the actuator count, control ranges, joint dimensions and the 0.5 ms timestep, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control target, loads no mesh or texture, resolves no contact, equality or tendon constraint (the six connect constraints and the three boxes are not simulated), simulates none of the gyro, accelerometer or magnetometer, and was never compared with the real engine. Snapshot and restore use the bridge's fallback copy of time, qpos, qvel and ctrl because the stand-in has no mj_getState or mj_setState. No physical Digit robot is modelled and no hardware was run; reviewed_by stays null. The fake is the class object fake.FakeMujoco (the bridge injects it as the mujoco module), so the gate reports the expected warnings G6.NOT_RECORDED, G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs seed, ticks and action.ctrl; there were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. The driver declares no limit of its own: the step limits are derived from the model (actuator_ctrlrange, source upstream_code) and no operator-required bound is needed. The package copies neither the model nor its stl assets and never imports the clone. Install is not run: environment.yaml:161 pins python=3.10.14, environment.yaml:252 mujoco==3.0.0 and setup.bash:23-32 downloads MuJoCo 2.10 from GitHub (network); fake.py is pure Python and the gate needs none of it.
